                                          | Photo Credit: special arrangement Gurupadagouda Sanganagouda Patil, four-time Congress MLA from Ron in Gadag district, was unanimously elected Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly on Friday. He is the 18th Speaker of the Assembly since 1972. Popularly known as G.S. Patil, his name was proposed by Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and seconded by Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara. The 78-year-old Mr. Patil comes from an agrarian political family. His elder brother, R.S. Patil, was a former MP who represented the Bagalkot constituency, while another brother, B.S. Patil, served as Chief Secretary of Karnataka during the S.M. Krishna government. He contested eight Assembly elections and won four. Mr. B.S. Patil was present at the officers’ gallery in the House today. A sportsperson, the newly elected Speaker was a wicketkeeper-batsman and played for the Mysore State team. He married Annapoorna in 1974 and has two sons and a daughter. His elder son, Prashanth, is a doctor, while his other son, Mithun, is a civil engineer. More than a dozen members spoke on Mr. Patil’s elevation as Speaker, describing him as a person who has donned many hats with equal ease. Besides being a politician, he is a farmer, educationist, sportsperson and cooperative leader. Mr. Patil, whose extended family is popularly known as the “Police Patil” or “Ron Gowdru” family, is the chairman of the Rajiv Gandhi Educational Institutions and is associated with various organisations in Gadag district. He has also held several positions in the cooperative sector. Former Minister H.K. Patil, MLA from Gadag, noted that prominent personalities such as Bharat Ratna awardee and Hindustani vocalist Pandit Bhimsen Joshi, classical musician Pandit Puttaraj Gawai and his father, K.H. Patil, hailed from Gadag district. Former Indian cricketer Sunil Joshi is also from the district. Pro-tem Speaker T.B. Jayachandra, who presided over the proceedings, declared Mr. Patil elected after a voice vote. Amid thumping of desks by members, Mr. Shivakumar, Leader of the Opposition R. Ashok, Mr. Jayachandra and Dr. Parameshwara accompanied Mr. Patil to the Speaker’s chair. The BJP boycotted the election, protesting against the Congress high command’s decision to communicate Mr. Patil’s name on AICC letterhead. Mr. Ashok said the Speaker was elected by the Assembly and not the AICC, and appealed to Mr. Patil to discharge his duties impartially. The post had fallen vacant following the resignation of U.T. Khader ahead of his induction into the Shivakumar-led Council of Ministers on June 3. Perhaps for the first time, presiding officers of both Houses hail from north Karnataka. title: Becky G's collaboration with Selena Gomez was totally unplanned - contactmusic.com
content: MUSIC NEWS FROM AROUND THE WORLD Becky G has revealed that her "surreal" collaboration with Benny Blanco and Selena Gomez on the track Te Olvido (La La) came about unintentionally. Becky G's collaboration with Benny Blanco and Selena Gomez came about by accident. The 29-year-old singer teamed up with the husband-and-wife duo on the new track Te Olvido (La La) and explained that the song was completely unplanned. Becky G told Rolling Stone: "It's just everything. I was trippin'. The Gomez girls, finally! She's the sweetest. "And I've known Benny for so long now, which is crazy. I remember the day we went into the studio, again, no intention set, just kind of like: 'Let's create and let's see what happens' "And I feel like it was a few weeks after, the song was so stuck in my head. I literally would wake up like: 'La, la, la la la, la, la, la, la la.' "And I'd walk around my house, and then I'd text my manager Ben, then I hit Benny, and be like: 'OK, so what are we gonna do with this song? What's gonna happen with the song?' And it just continued to unfold." She went on to add: "I remember hearing Sel's verse on it, and hearing our voices together was so surreal. And then we shot our music video. "And it was so wild, because I shot the EPA music video around the same time. "Literally it was like a three-day span where we had shot the EPA music video and then we also did our music video. Everybody's like: 'Damn, Becky's really out here. What's going on? Like we wanna know the tea.' The collaboration with Gomez comes after Becky confessed she doesn't see other female artists as competition. The Shower singer - who has a particularly close friendship with Karol G - has revealed she hates it when female artists are pitted against each other. Speaking about her relationship with the Provenza singer, Becky told CBS Mornings: "We have a beautiful friendship, one I’m really, really thankful for, and one that I think throughout the years, we’ve really earned with one another. "I think that’s for many, many reasons … through experiences, shared experiences, individual experiences and, of course, an industry that is so quick to pit people against each other." Becky scoffed at the idea that Karol is an adversary. Asked if they're rivals, she said: "Absolutely not. No. "I mean, for me, personally, my greatest competition is the person I look at in the mirror every morning, you know? And I know she feels the same way for herself. "Our goal is to be the best versions of ourselves, and it’s been beautiful to kind of grow up in this friendship as well, and see someone literally just not only break down every door, but also hold it open for others to come through." title: The Adventure Bike That Owners Keep Longer Than Expected - Top Speed
content: Abhik has been an automotive journalist for over a decade, with expertise in both motorcycle and car road testing, reviewing, as well as writing and executing feature travelogs. He has worked for Indian brands including Evo India Magazine, Auto Today by India Today Group, and anchored video reviews for Powerdrift Studios. He also has keen interests in most forms of motorsports, having competed in a couple of seasons of one-make racing with TVS Racing on two wheels and Volkswagen Motorsport on four. Alongside his motoring pursuits, e-sports and sim racing are current interests, as are cycling and cycling tech. Today’s tech-led motorcycling world is so fast-paced that model progression year-on-year can not just be quick, but also jump forward substantially. Honda proved as much with a single-generation swap where the 2019 CRF1000L Africa Twin was replaced by the CRF1100L in 2020, which was leaps and bounds forward in tech. It came with a higher 1,084cc displacement, a six-axis IMU, and a touchscreen. What this does is create a buyer response of wanting the latest and greatest rather than sticking to the older model, which would still serve for years mechanically. But every now and then, a product comes along that challenges established norms, and a BMW flagship adventure bike sets the example of one. Switching bikes costs more than money. Romanticizing the love for motorcycles is one thing, but a pragmatic perspective will tell you that a rider who has logged a decent number of miles on one machine has spent ample time with it to have subconsciously calibrated its nuances. And these are details that are now muscle memory. Stuff like how much front brake force the fork takes up before the nose dives aggressively, and exactly where the pegs touch down through a tight corner to have a mental map of the bike's grip limits. A new bike may be mechanically different, and these nuances take a bit of a learning curve to establish again. The learning curve is a non-issue, and is what helps you build skills in a motorcycling discipline of choice. It’s the findings that may lead to a mental comparison and the possible regret of getting a new machine that doesn’t live up to the old one. For some riders, especially those who spend a lot of saddle time traversing unforgiving terrains where support or help can be scarce, these factors matter more than the latest tech on offer. The trust and knowledge of a bike well established in the rider’s mind are what prevent one from scratching the itch for a new bike. In the ADV space, there’s only one bike that resonates with this logic. At $17,995 to start, the BMW R 1250 GS wasn't cheap when BMW sold it new between 2019 and 2023, before the R 1300 GS pushed it out of the current lineup. Used listings today run closer to $13,700 to $16,000, depending on mileage and options. But it’s not the great resale value that makes owners hold onto the bike. Underneath, a 1,254cc boxer twin uses BMW's ShiftCam variable valve timing that’s good for 136 hp and 105 lb-ft, output that hasn't aged into irrelevance despite a five-year-old engine. Riders who bought one when it was new are, in plenty of cases, still riding it and there are yet more reasons why. BMW's ShiftCam variable valve timing is what makes that output possible, switching cam profiles depending on specific load and rpm. But the ownership costs are what make the R 1250 GS all the more appealing. Valve clearance rarely needs correcting even after 100,000 kilometers on this engine, and mechanics who've opened one up at that mileage report pistons, cylinders, and the crankshaft all still looking relatively factory-fresh. BMW calls for an inspection of the shaft drive at 12,500 miles and swaps it out preventively around 37,000, even footing that replacement bill itself for as long as the owner keeps the bike. That’s a huge plus in itself. A boxer engine and a drivetrain that both hold up that well simply don't give an owner a reason to trade in the bike on mechanical grounds alone. BMW’s unique telelever front end, something you’ll often hear GS owners brag about, soaks up 7.5 inches of travel through a design BMW has refined since the 1990s. It trades the dive of a conventional fork for a setup that stays composed under hard braking no matter the model year. Chassis composure aside, the electronics are still current. Standard equipment included a 6.5-inch TFT display, a full LED headlight, and Hill Start Control, along with two riding modes, Rain and Road. An optional Riding Modes Pro package added Dynamic, Dynamic Pro, Enduro, and Enduro Pro, offering six settings in total. It’s no wonder then that the R 1250 GS is still highly regarded as the ultimate ADV. Another reason that the R 1250 GS is preferred as a used buy is that BMW never sold the R 1250 GS as a single, fixed setup. Seat height ranges from a standard 33.5 to 34.3 inches down to 31.5 to 32.3 inches with the factory low-suspension option, and BMW offered a wider spread of factory seat heights on top of that. So a younger rider who has the flexibility to tolerate a taller seat may only have to switch saddles and/or suspension 10 or 15 years down the line, instead of switching bikes altogether. At 476 pounds, the weight is still manageable with room for a passenger, a full set of panniers, and a top case. BMW has even gone ahead and thought of making things easier for the rider with the optional Dynamic ESA electronic suspension. It adjusts on the fly, softening up for a loaded touring run and firming back up for a solo commute. And this is what makes the R 1250 GS so versatile for speed, comfort and everyday use if so desired. A 2017 Triumph Tiger Explorer 1200 undercuts the GS on the used market, typically running around $9,540. Its 1,215cc inline-triple makes 137 horsepower and 89 lb-ft, more of both than the boxer twin, and a shaft final drive keeps its own maintenance low the same way the GS's does. What it can't match is the GS's specific legacy and pedigree for round-the-world travel. The GS, after all, defined adventure riding for the modern motorcyclist. A brand new 2026 Harley-Davidson Pan America 1250 Special is the kind of bike that makes a five-year-old GS feel old on paper. It starts at $19,999, and its 1,252cc Revolution Max V-twin makes 150 horsepower and 94 lb-ft, wrapped in a platform that didn't exist when the R 1250 GS was already several years into production. That's exactly the pitch aimed at a GS owner shopping for something newer. The Pan America has only been on sale since 2021, though; it isn't much time to build the kind of ownership history the GS enjoys. Both rivals pull in a different direction, with the Tiger on long-distance capability and the Pan America being newer and stronger on paper. But neither can borrow the GS's sheer globe-trotting legacy, and the long-distance trips that built the name or the high-mileage ownership culture that keeps this generation off the used lots and in their owners’ garages longer than most. title: GS Patil elected Karnataka Assembly Speaker; BJP, JD(S) boycott election - The Federal
content: Bengaluru, Aug 14 (PTI) Congress MLA Gurupadagouda Sanganagouda Patil was elected Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly on Friday. Popularly known as G S Patil, his name was proposed by Chief Minister D K Shivakumar and seconded by Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara. Pro-tem Speaker T B Jayachandra, who presided over the proceedings, declared Patil elected after a voice vote. The opposition BJP and JD(S) boycotted the Speaker election, and were not present in the House during the process. The post fell vacant following the resignation of U T Khader ahead of his induction into the Shivakumar-led Council of Ministers on June 3. Patil is a four-time MLA from the Ron Assembly constituency in Gadag district. A member of the Lingayat community, he previously served as chairman of the Karnataka Mineral Development Corporation and Karnataka Renewable Energy Development Ltd. Ahead of the Speaker election, Leader of Opposition in the Assembly R Ashoka had announced the BJP and JD(S)'s decision to boycott the process in protest against the ruling Congress "unconstitutionally" naming the new Speaker on its official letterhead. He told reporters that the Congress was starting a new tradition in the country and the state by announcing the Speaker's name on its party letterhead, thereby undermining the sovereignty of the House and the rights of its elected representatives. He was referring to the Congress high command's letter to CM D K Shivakumar on August 3, which contained the names of 19 ministers to be inducted into his Cabinet. The letter also contained the names of the party's nominees for the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman and Deputy Chairman posts. Ashoka had also made it clear that once the Speaker was elected, the BJP and JD(S) would accord the Speaker's chair and office all due respect. Accordingly, once Patil was declared elected as the Speaker, all BJP and JD(S) members came to the House. LoP Ashoka even joined the CM in escorting the new Speaker to his chair. Addressing the House after taking over the responsibility of the Speaker, Patil said he wants to implement a paperless legislature 'e-Vidhana,' using technology as soon as possible. He also said that the practice of providing good training for MLAs would continue. Thanking the House and its members for electing him as the Speaker, he assured that he would try to live up to the expectations placed on him and make an honest effort to ensure the smooth conduct of the proceedings, according to the rules, taking everyone along. Expressing gratitude to the people of his Ron constituency, the new Speaker said "Four decades after beginning his political journey at Ron Purasabha, I have occupied the highest seat in this House. This is the beauty of democracy." For the Speaker, the only party is that of the Constitution, not the ruling or opposition party, he said, "The success of democracy doesn't lie in majority, but in the respect given to the voice of the Opposition." Speaking after the Speaker's election in the Assembly, CM Shivakumar said the Congress high command had not unilaterally declared the Speaker's name but had only named the party's nominee for the position in a letter written to him. He said the opposition has taken a "political stand". "The Speaker's chair is not a personal seat. Our party leaders recommended a party nominee for this position; they did not unilaterally declare the Speaker. The opposition leaders are protesting this by boycotting. Whoever becomes Speaker is above party lines and must listen to everyone. Therefore, the opposition should have participated in the Speaker's election instead of protesting. Protesting does not suit their dignity,” he opined. Speaking about the Speaker, the CM highlighted that he belonged to a prominent agricultural family, which has served the society for decades. "You (Patil) have been in politics with us for many years... Your brother R.S. Patil served as a Member of Parliament. Another brother serves in the cooperative sector, and the other brother served in the Health Department. One of your brothers is B.S. Patil, who served as the Chief Secretary of the state. Your younger brother is the DCC Bank President. Your entire family has served society in this manner," he said. LoP Ashoka sepaking in the Assembly, said declaring the Speaker's name on a Congress letterhead is not a good precedent, as it is a constitutional post. The Speaker post belongs to the House and no blemish should be attached to it. By announcing the Speaker's name on party letterhead, the ruling Congress disrespected the post, he alleged, adding, "Such decisions (Speaker election) are not made in the party office, but in the House (Assembly)... What if instructions also start coming to the Speaker's office on party letterheads? Will there be respect? That's our concern," he added. Wishing Patil the best, Ashoka said the expectation from the new Speaker is that the Speaker’s Chair should stand above party politics. The Constitution should be held in greater esteem than any party letterhead. The Rules of Procedure of the House should take precedence over instructions from the government or the party. title: Becky G's new album 'marries' both sides of her personality - Female First
content: Becky G's new album reflects both sides of her personality. The 29-year-old singer has just released Baraja Bendita, her fifth studio album, and Becky feels proud of the record because it's honest to every side of her personality. The chart-topping star - whose real name is Rebbeca Gomez - told CBS Mornings: "I feel like this album really marries the Rebbecca side of me ... the sensual, more vulnerable side of me, the intimate side of me, and then also, you know, who I am. "The boss in the boardroom and the boss on the stage." Becky's album title loosely translates to, a blessed deck of cards. And the singer claims that she's "gotten really good at playing the game" during the course of her career. She said: "We all know that quote of we can't necessarily control the cards that we were dealt – but what we can control is how we play them. "I feel like throughout my years of, of doing what I do, personally and professionally, I've gotten really good at playing the game and I think that that's something that especially as women, as we've become more empowered, we're almost taught to feel more shameful about that and I think I'm just owning it." Becky previously admitted to feeling isolated during the early years of her music career. The singer - who was born to American parents of Mexican descent - recalled being the "youngest" and the "only brown girl in the room" at various points in her career. Becky - who released her debut album, Mala Santa, in 2019 - told Interview magazine: "This industry can be very lonely, and sometimes I really crave a connection with people who really understand what it is to be in my shoes. "For so long, I was the youngest person, or the only woman, or the only brown girl in the room. I felt isolating. So finding artists who understand the hard work and sacrifice that comes with success makes all of it feel more meaningful."

content: SGA Solutions has obtained Good Software (GS) certification for its zero trust-based integrated identity, credential, and access management (ICAM) solution. ​SGA Solutions said Aug. 13 that its “SGA ZTA ICAM” became the first ICAM solution in South Korea to receive GS certification. ​GS certification is a nationally recognized software quality certification that comprehensively evaluates software functionality, reliability, and usability. SGA Solutions said the certification demonstrates that the solution meets software quality standards required by public institutions and other organizations. ​As the adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) expands, the need to manage not only user accounts but also non-human identities (NHIs), including service accounts and application programming interface (API) accounts, is growing. As the use of AI agents increases, the number of digital accounts and access privileges that companies must manage internally is also expected to rise. ​SGA ZTA ICAM integrates account, authentication, and authorization management, and access-policy functions based on user and account information. It establishes user accounts as a new security perimeter, grants each user the minimum required privileges, and continuously verifies access activity. For security personnel managing large numbers of accounts, the platform provides user-information collection and distribution, process management, threat analysis, and self-service functions through a single platform. ​In a zero trust environment, ICAM serves as the policy decision point (PDP). It establishes access policies based on users’ identities and authorization information and distributes them to individual systems to implement the principle of least privilege and continuous verification. ​SGA Solutions plans to use the GS certification as a springboard to expand its ICAM business across various industries, including public institutions, financial services, and manufacturing.

Following the entry-level class comes the mid-range segment: a 600-cc touring enduro bearing the legendary ‘GS’ designation and featuring an in-line twin engine will enable BMW to target new customer groups. The response came from the heart of British motor racing: ‘Together we are strong!’ SPEEDWEEK.com readers had known this for some time: a few weeks before BMW unveiled its new entry-level range, the F 450 GS, in Milan, BMW Motorrad boss Markus Flasch had already hinted, in a conversation with editor-in-chief Ivo Schützbach, that the Bavarian development engineers would be taking another close look at the new F 450 platform for the next expansion of the model range. As we were also able to report for the first time shortly afterwards, this new iteration of the parallel-twin engine will debut in a lightweight touring enduro, with which BMW is targeting customers of Yamaha’s best-selling Ténéré 700 and will be bringing the legendary ‘GS’ designation into a new market segment. Initial photos of an early test prototype now reveal for the first time the approach the Bavarian manufacturer intends to take to make its mark in the segment between the F 450 GS and the F 900 GS: The touring enduro shows clear technical parallels with the F 450 GS and draws on a similar approach for the exhaust system and chassis components. The rear shock absorber mounting, for example, is similar to that of its little sister, and the swingarm is of a similar design. Yet the differences are also clear: the motorbike is fitted with a 21-inch front wheel and an 18-inch rear wheel, and looks considerably more grown-up than its by no means petite little sister. The steel bridge frame on the prototype is also more closely modelled on the F 900 GS, and the braking system resembles that of its big sister. The fairing parts also reveal that the bike is still at an early stage of development, yet many design details are already finely crafted. For instance, the headlight will apparently be modelled on that of its big sister, the R 1300 GS, although the characteristic ‘beak’ is still missing. At the same time, the design details that are still missing reveal that development is far from complete. The name is also still up in the air: ‘F 600 GS’ would fit into the BMW nomenclature, whilst a revival of the ‘F 650 GS’ or ‘F 700’ designations would also be a logical possibility. In any case, actual engine capacity would not be a determining factor for the name: the F 800 and F 900 GS, for example, use the same engine and therefore have the same cylinder capacity. That’s not very specific, but a look at the current BMW model range reveals a large gap between 420 and 895 cubic centimetres of displacement, and a look at BMW’s partner TVS also helps. The Indian company manufactures the F450 range on behalf of BMW and has also just brought a bored-out version of the parallel-twin to production for the ‘Atlas’ from its British subsidiary Norton, thereby demonstrating the development potential of the engine. In the Indo-British variants, the Atlas and Atlas GT, the BMW engine – in a heavily revised form – delivers a displacement of 585 cubic centimetres and 70 PS. Four weeks ago, Aprilia headed into the summer break from Germany with a badly injured Marco Bezzecchi. The response came from the heart of British motor racing: ‘Together we are strong!’ The engine in BMW’s mid-range GS differs from that of the Norton in several respects in our photos, whilst others show similarities. The internal workings will certainly differ: the British model, for example, uses a crankshaft with the 270-degree ignition offset typical of this class, whilst the BMW F450 GS employs an unorthodox 135-degree crankpin offset. Reportedly, the displacement of the BMW and Norton is said to be on a par, and the rated power output is also likely to be comparable, depending on the final design of the engine: This would mean between 65 and 70 PS for the Bavarian model, placing it just below the class benchmark, the Yamaha Ténéré 700. Last but not least, there is the question of the launch date: the test bike shows that BMW still has some development work to do on the new mid-range GS. A launch is therefore not expected before 2028. title: GS Global spurs North American energy sector with new Houston office - The Korea Times
content: From left, GS Global U.S. President Lee Jun-hak, Jindal Pipe U.S. President Vikas Chandra, Korean Consul General in Houston Lee Kyung-eun, GS Global Corp. Head of Steel Department and Senior Vice President Kim Jung-hoon, Brown Strauss President and CEO Kris Farris and GS Global U.S. Houston Branch General Manager Park Jun-hee join a ribbon-cutting event during the opening ceremony for  GS Global Houston Branch in the United States, Tuesday (local time). Courtesy of GS Global Energy and infrastructure accelerator GS Global has opened a new branch in Houston, strengthening its local sales capabilities as it targets growing opportunities in North America’s energy and infrastructure markets. The company held an opening ceremony on Tuesday (local time) in Uptown, one of Houston’s major commercial districts. Attendees included Korean Consul General in Houston Lee Kyung-eun, representatives from key customers such as Jindal USA and major Korean and international companies including POSCO, Hyundai Steel, Korea National Oil Corporation and Hanwha Ocean. The establishment of the Houston branch reflects GS Global’s strategic decision to respond proactively to rising demand for project-based steel products driven by increased investment in energy, power generation and infrastructure across the United States. Demand for high-quality steel products has expanded particularly rapidly as construction of artificial intelligence data centers and investment in power infrastructure accelerate nationwide. GS Global has been operating its U.S. business primarily through its Los Angeles-based subsidiary. However, amid strengthened protectionist trade policies and the ongoing restructuring of global supply chains, the company decided to establish an additional base in Houston, a key hub for the U.S. energy industry. The Houston branch will go beyond importing and selling steel products. Its key responsibilities will include identifying demand for project-based steel, supporting project acquisition, participating in the U.S. energy industry’s value chain and expanding into related business areas such as energy, chemicals and shipbuilding equipment. The branch also plans to maximize cooperation with major Korean steelmakers that have operations near Houston, including Hyundai Steel and Dongkuk Steel. It will also seek new business partners among local engineering, procurement and construction companies and steel fabricators. During the second half of this year, GS Global will focus on establishing local networks, strengthening project pipeline management and stabilizing the branch’s operations. Beginning in 2027, it plans to expand project acquisition support and identify new business opportunities, with the goal of developing the Houston branch into a core hub for business development in the southern U.S. “Establishing the Houston branch is a strategic investment aimed at expanding our contact points with customers in the U.S. market and strengthening our practical sales capabilities,” a GS Global representative said. “We will identify diverse new opportunities, including project-based steel businesses, and establish a sustainable foundation for growth in North America.” With the opening of the Houston branch, GS Global now operates a global network of 23 overseas offices and entities across 16 countries. In the U.S., the company will enhance its market responsiveness through its Los Angeles subsidiary and the new Houston branch.

Popularly known as G. S. Patil, his name was proposed by Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar and seconded by Deputy CM G. Parameshwara. Pro-tem Speaker T. B. Jayachandra, who presided over the proceedings, declared Mr. Patil elected after a voice vote. The opposition BJP and JD(S) boycotted the election of the Speaker. The post fell vacant following the resignation of U. T. Khader ahead of his induction into the Shivakumar-led Council of Ministers on June 3. Mr. Patil is a four-time MLA from the Ron Assembly constituency in Gadag district. A member of the Lingayat community, he previously served as chairperson of the Karnataka Mineral Development Corporation and Karnataka Renewable Energy Development Limited. Senior Member of Legislative Council Saleem Ahmed was elected as Chairperson of the Upper House on August 14. Seniormost member and former chairperson Basavaraj Horatti, whose resignation caused the vacancy, was among those who greeted the Congress leader following the election. Speaking to reporters on Thursday, Leader of Opposition in the Assembly R Ashoka said the BJP and JD(S) had decided to boycott the Speaker election in protest against the ruling Congress "unconstitutionally" naming the new Speaker on its official letterhead. He accused the Congress of starting a new tradition in the country and the State by announcing the Speaker's name on its party letterhead, thereby undermining the sovereignty of the House and the rights of its elected representatives. He was referring to the Congress high command's letter to CM D. K. Shivakumar on August 3, which contained the names of 19 ministers to be inducted into his Cabinet. The letter also contained the names of the party's nominees for the post of Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Assembly, Chairperson, and Deputy Chairperson of the Council. Mr. Ashok had also made it clear that once the Speaker was elected, the BJP and JD(S) would accord the Speaker's chair and office all due respect. Ahead of the Speaker's election, the CM introduced his new Cabinet ministers to the House. This is the first Assembly session after the Shivakumar-led Cabinet took charge. title: 12 BMW Motorcycles Worth Every Penny - Top Speed
content: In the American motorcycle market, BMW Motorrad offers one of the most diverse lineups of bikes. These range from luxury tourers to do-it-all adventure bikes to retro-vibing roadsters and track-going monsters. At the same time, BMW surprisingly keeps the value quotient in check (particularly from a European bikemaker context), and most of its bikes are worth each penny you pay. We're talking about 12 such bikes, ranging from touring bikes with Japanese reliability to adventure bikes that excel at everything. There's something for everyone here. BMW offers the best of two-wheeled luxury, comfort, and performance with the K 1600 GTL. This full dresser brings the best of "big" American luxury charm with sophisticated technology to offer a surprisingly versatile land yacht. A unique six-cylinder engine powers the K 1600 GTL. This 1,649 cc mill produces 160 horsepower at 6,750 RPM and 132.7 pound-feet at 5,250 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual coupled to a final shaft drive system. For the chassis, a cast-aluminum bridge-type frame is present. It is suspended on BMW's famed Duolever front suspension with a central spring strut and 4.5 inches of travel. The rear gets the Paralever setup, coupled to a cast-iron single-sided swingarm and 5.3 inches of travel. Technology features are galore, too. Notable ones include a huge 10.25-inch TFT, a four-button cluster for custom functions, dynamic traction control, three ride modes, dynamic electronic suspension, hill start control, heated grips and seats, and an audio system, among others. This is arguably the most value-packed luxury touring motorcycle, and it undercuts the Honda Gold Wing, despite being more powerful. The 1,649 cc mill mentioned above is present here as well, in the same exact tune. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual and a final shaft drive neatly hidden in its single-sided swingarm. The chassis is also similar to the GTL, featuring the bridge-type cast aluminum frame. As for suspension, the front gets a double-wishbone (Duolever) with 4.5 inches of travel. The rear gets a monoshock (Paralever) setup with 5.3 inches of travel. The suspension offers electronic adjustability and even an automatic load-leveling feature. There is no dearth of top-spec technology. The K 1600 B gets a huge 10.25-inch TFT with a wide range of connectivity and integrated map navigation features. Other notable features include three ride modes, dynamic traction control, hill start control, and engine brake control, among others. If you’d rather pick an old-school full-dress tourer than one of the new-age ones, then BMW’s R 18 Transcontinental is worth a look. Taking the fight straight to Harley-Davidson’s Grand American Tourers, this full-dress Beemer builds on the R 18 cruiser with every luxury touring essential you’ll ever need and then some. It makes for a first-class touring experience that will have you looking forward to every touring opportunity. It’s powered by a big boxer engine that delivers at least 110 pound-feet of torque between 2,000 and 4,000 RPM. Other touring bits include a relaxed riding posture, a massive fairing with deflectors, high-quality saddlebags and a topcase with available central locking, and available active cruise control. It also gets a large TFT display paired with 4 traditional analog gauges, with an available Marshall sound system. It’s a unique German take on a formula that’s otherwise very American. Also, the Pope has one! This futuristic-looking touring bike makes luxury feel practical. The same boxer twin powers the R 1300 RT as on the go-anywhere R 1300 GS. The 1,300 cc mill produces 145 horsepower at 7,750 RPM and 110 pound-feet of torque at 6,500 RPM, sent to the wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox coupled to a final Cardan shaft drive system for added durability. Underpinning the R 1300 RT is a two-part frame with the engine utilized as a stressed member. It is suspended on BMW's famed Telelever front and Paralever rear suspension setups with 5.8 inches of front and 6.2 inches of rear travel. Adding to its versatility is a factory-adjustable seat, solid wind protection, and commendable technology. Notable features include keyless ride, dynamic electronic stability control, heated grips, and a gorgeous-looking 10.25-inch TFT with Bluetooth navigation as standard. This BMW adventure bike is famed for being a flagship that can do it all exceptionally well. Powering the flagship GS is the 1,300 cc liquid-cooled mill, which produces 145 horsepower at 7,750 RPM and 110 pound-feet at 6,500 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a standard six-speed manual with a final Cardan shaft drive system. It can also be equipped with an optional automatic transmission. Underpinning the R 1300 GS is a sophisticated setup. It comprises a pressed-steel main frame utilizing the engine as a stressed member. It is suspended on a double-wishbone suspension setup up front with 7.5 inches of travel. The rear gets a link-type monoshock with 7.8 inches of travel. BMW has loaded the R 1300 GS to the brim with technology features. Notable ones include four ride modes, dynamic traction control, dynamic brake control, dynamic cruise control, and hill start control. The dashboard comprises a sizable 6.5-inch TFT. The BMW S 1000 RR is a surprisingly affordable sports bike that is cheaper than a Honda Fireblade. Powering the S 1000 RR is a proven inline-four engine that produces 205 horsepower at 13,000 RPM and 83 pound-feet of torque at 11,000 RPM. It is coupled to a WSBK-derived quick throttle as standard as part of its latest update. Underpinning the flagship BMW sportbike is a lightweight twin-spar aluminum frame, coupled to a race-derived aluminum swingarm and subframe. The frame is suspended on 45 mm inverted front forks with 4.7 inches of travel, alongside a monoshock with 4.6 inches of travel. Both ends offer full adjustability. Cutting-edge technology such as six ride modes, pit lane limiter, launch control, dynamic traction control, wheelie control, and slide control is present, too. This BMW crossover feels worth every dollar because it blends urban mobility, highway runs, and even spirited mountain sessions so seamlessly. The S 1000 XR packs a proper superbike engine derived from the S 1000 RR. The 999 cc liquid-cooled inline-four mill produces 170 horsepower at 11,000 RPM and 84 pound-feet of torque at 9,250 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox. Underpinnings comprise a bridge-type cast aluminum frame, using the engine as a load-bearer, suspended on long-travel springs. The front gets 45 mm inverted forks with 5.9 inches of travel, and the rear comprises a monoshock with 5.9 inches of travel. Its electronic, self-adjusting rebound settings at both ends instill sharp cornering confidence. Technology features are plentiful and stitch its do-it-all character together. This is BMW's arch-nemesis to the Triumph Scrambler 1200. The R 12 G/S is powered by a mighty 1,170 cc boxer twin engine with 109 horsepower at 7,000 RPM and 85 pound-feet of torque at 6,500 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox coupled to a final Cardan shaft drive system for added durability. The engine sits in a tubular space frame and is suspended on long-travel suspension. The front gets 45 mm inverted forks with 8.2 inches of travel, and the rear gets a monoshock with 7.8 inches of travel. Both ends are fully adjustable. This is further complemented by durable aluminum cross-spoke wheels wrapped with all-terrain tires. The R 12 G/S gets a slew of assistive technology features. Notable ones include riding modes, dynamic traction control, cornering ABS, dynamic engine brake control, and partial integral brake system. This classic cruiser bike matches the essence of American big twins but with a unique twist: a large air-oil-cooled boxer-twin engine instead of a V-twin. In fact, it is the largest production motorcycle flat twin until the much-anticipated production-spec R 20 breaks cover. The 1,802 cc mill produces 91 horsepower at 4,750 RPM and 120 pound-feet of torque at 3,000 RPM. Adding to its heavy-duty outlook is a double-loop steel main frame with bolted beams. A twin-sided steel swing arm is part of the chassis and adds to its stretched-out stance. The R 18 gets telescopic forks up front with 4.7 inches of travel. The rear comprises a hidden monoshock that seems to be strongly inspired by the Harley Softail series. Owing to its old-school charm, BMW has added very little technology to the R 18, with notable features being LED lighting and a USB Type-C port only. This is a gravely overlooked BMW naked bike that offers grin-worthy performance at a bargain price. It is powered by the same 999 cc inline-four liquid-cooled engine as the S 1000 RR, but subtracts the ShiftCam for a more peaky output of 170 horsepower at 11,000 RPM and 84 pound-feet of torque at 9,250 RPM. Power is sent to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual gearbox coupled to a standard slipper clutch. The banking industry is witnessing a structural shift toward active ETFs and options-based income products, as investors increasingly seek higher income, tax efficiency and downside-risk management within the liquid ETF wrapper. Derivative-income ETFs have grown to roughly $180 billion in assets, seeing a CAGR of more than 70% since 2021, according to Goldman's official press release citing Morningstar. Against this backdrop, The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. GS has agreed to acquire NEOS Investments for consideration of up to $2.25 billion in cash and equity, subject to certain performance and service commitments. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, pending regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. The acquisition will add $30 billion in assets across NEOS' 19 options-based income ETFs to Goldman Sachs Asset Management's existing $40 billion in income and outcome-oriented options-based ETF solutions. Once complete, the deal will make Goldman Sachs Asset Management the eighth-largest active ETF provider. The NEOS purchase follows Goldman's acquisition of Innovator Capital Management, and together the deals create a broad options-based ETF franchise spanning buffer, managed outcome and income strategies. As of June 30, 2026, Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Innovator from Goldman Sachs Asset Management and NEOS manage more than $130 billion in ETF assets under supervision. Overall, Goldman Sachs' push into options-based ETFs is likely to enhance its competitive advantage by giving the firm greater scale, a broader range of differentiated products and stronger exposure to fast-growing active ETF categories. The addition of NEOS, alongside Innovator, strengthens Goldman's presence across income, buffer and managed-outcome strategies, helping it compete more effectively for investor assets. At the same time, the expansion should support higher recurring fee revenues and further diversify its Asset & Wealth Management business. Competition has been intensifying for Goldman as banks like Morgan Stanley MS and JPMorgan JPM are expanding crypto-related capabilities even if they have not yet launched proprietary ETFs. Morgan Stanley has filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission to launch ETFs linked to Bitcoin and Solana. The proposed products — the Morgan Stanley Bitcoin Trust and the Morgan Stanley Solana Trust — are designed to give investors direct price exposure to the two cryptocurrencies without requiring them to own or store the tokens themselves. JPMorgan has taken a broader, infrastructure-led approach to crypto and blockchain. The bank offers crypto trading services to institutional clients and has built out custody capabilities, while also piloting on-chain settlement and tokenized deposits through its blockchain unit, Onyx. JPMorgan has launched blockchain-based platforms for wholesale payments and repo transactions, enabling faster and more efficient settlement using tokenized assets. title: State Department expands push to reclassify employees as at-will workers - Government Executive
content:
The State Department is expanding its search for employees to reclassify as at-will workers under the Trump administration’s new Schedule Policy/Career designation
                  
                    J. David Ake/Getty Images The State Department is taking another look at its workforce to see if more employees should fall under a new governmentwide designation that makes them easier to fire. Agency officials are expanding their search for employees to reclassify as at-will workers under the Trump administration’s new Schedule Policy/Career designation for the federal workforce. President Donald Trump signed an executive order in June that officially reclassified 8,000 federal employees into Schedule Policy/Career, a rebranding of the Schedule F designation that Trump pursued in his first term, but did not implement before leaving office. Employees placed into the new schedule would no longer be able to challenge adverse personnel actions before the Merit Systems Protection Board, and whistleblower complaints filed by Schedule P/C employees would be investigated by their own agency, rather than the Office of Special Counsel. The Office of Personnel Management previously estimated that about 50,000 federal employees would fall under this new job category. But an OPM spokesperson said in June that the administration chose to instead focus on “the most senior-level career policy officials.” The State Department’s actions suggest that its initial reclassification of employees fell short of the White House’s expectations, and other agencies may take a similar approach. NOTUS first reported that the Trump administration is directing agencies to find more federal employees to convert to Schedule P/C. A spokesperson for the foreign policy agency declined to comment on “internal deliberative personnel matters.” One State Department employee told Government Executive that human resources officials are using a short questionnaire to determine if GS-13 and GS-14 level employees are working in policymaking positions that should be reclassified to Schedule P/C. “It is not clear how many ‘yes’ responses would trigger a new Schedule P/C status,” the employee said. The questionnaire asks if a position “formulates, develops and/or determines foreign policy, including creation of draft documents with policy recommendations," or "develops or reviews non-public Executive Orders, regulations, directives, policy memoranda, or deliberative materials protected by the deliberative process privilege regarding foreign policy." Other screening questions ask if an employee “provides substantive advocacy of foreign policy,” or represents the department before Congress, the Office of Management and Budget, foreign governments or external organizations regarding the administration’s foreign policy. The questionnaire asks if an employee “publicly advocates Administration foreign policy through official communications or media engagement” or “exercises delegated authority to commit or bind the Department to policy decisions." The department is also looking for positions that conduct official bargaining or negotiations on behalf of the department, or whether an employee “performs statutory policy-making responsibilities." The State Department has already shifted supervisory foreign affairs officers and specialists, as well as other senior-level positions, to Schedule Policy/Career. A second State staffer said the department is still in the early stages of its expanded search for Schedule P/C conversions, but added that this work is “moving relatively fast.” Staff have been directed to update to their position descriptions to ensure they reflect the full scope of their responsibilities. “GS-13s, I don’t think, are typically in a position that you’re going to think of as a senior policymaking position,” the employee said. “I was surprised, personally, to see positions that junior given this designation.” A senior administration official told reporters in June that 97% of employees that fall under Schedule Policy/Career are at a GS-15 level or higher. The official said a “small number” of GS-13 and GS-14 employees were also converted, but that most of them work at OMB. “Outside of OMB, there are very, very few positions that are below the level of GS-15 that are being covered,” the administration official said. “The bottom line is that almost all of these are very senior positions in the federal government.” The administration official said Schedule Policy/Career would “increase the accountability of officials who are responsible for carrying out the elected president’s policy agenda,” but would have little day-to-day impact on reclassified employees. “As long as they’re performing their job duties in a competent, professional manner, they have nothing to be afraid of,” the official said. The second State Department employee said Schedule P/C’s impact on the workforce has not yet been fully felt, but suggested that newly at-will employees may be reluctant to offer candid feedback on policy matters. “If you convert my position to a position that can be expeditiously removed, I’m going to more carefully tailor what I’m saying,” they said. “Its practical effect, I think it’s safe to assume, is that it will reduce people’s willingness to give advice or offer policy positions that are inconsistent with the direction of the administration.” A third individual said the department has started reviewing GS-13 and GS-14 positions for “possible conversion to Schedule Policy/Career.” “That process has resulted in a hold on reclassifying any of the thousands of GS-13 and 14 positions, which an office or bureau might otherwise do from time to time to align position grades with updated responsibilities,” the individual said. OPM's guidance to agencies states that many aspects of federal employment – including rules around pay, leave, benefits and reductions in force – remain unchanged for those moved to Schedule P/C. OPM also included a sample termination notice agencies may use when firing Schedule P/C employees. In the template, agencies may specify “unacceptable performance or misconduct” as justification for an employee's termination. title: Bespin Global’s AI Platform Wins Grade 1 GS Certification - thelec.net
content: The “HelpNow Agentic AI Platform v4.0,” an artificial intelligence (AI) agent platform developed by AI services and solutions company Bespin Global, has received Grade 1 Good Software (GS) certification from the Telecommunications Technology Association (TTA). ​Bespin Global plans to use the certification to strengthen its public-sector business. The company will expand direct adoption channels by registering the platform on the government’s KONEPS comprehensive shopping mall, add AI agent templates tailored to public-sector areas such as administration, welfare, and safety, and optimize the platform for the public G-Cloud environment. ​Bespin Global describes the HelpNow Agentic AI Platform as an integrated AI transformation (AX) platform for building, deploying, and operating enterprise AI agents based on generative AI. ​According to Bespin Global, the platform is based on a model-independent architecture that allows flexible use of various large language models (LLMs). It supports inference, tool integration, workflow execution, application programming interface (API) integration, and external-service calls based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP). ​Bespin Global also said the product can minimize hallucinations in generative AI and improve the accuracy and reliability of responses through its proprietary agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), few-shot training, and dynamic-prompt technologies. ​The HelpNow Agentic AI Platform has also obtained ISO/IEC 42001 certification, an international standard for artificial intelligence management systems, and has been adopted by organizations including the National Pension Service, the Ulsan Metropolitan Office of Education, and the Ministry of the Interior and Safety’s “Modu-ui Gwangjang” platform.

title: GS Global opens Houston branch to expand North American energy, infrastructure business - Korea JoongAng Daily
content: The trading company opened a Houston branch to expand steel sales and project business across North America’s energy and infrastructure sectors. GS Global opened a new branch in Houston on Tuesday to strengthen its local sales presence in North America’s energy and infrastructure markets, the company said Thursday. GS Global has previously operated its U.S. business primarily through its Los Angeles subsidiary. The new Houston branch is aimed at responding to growing demand for steel for major projects amid surging investment in energy, power and infrastructure across the United States. The branch plans to expand its business beyond steel imports and sales. It will also focus on identifying demand and supporting bids for project-based steel orders, participating in the U.S. energy industry value chain and expanding into steel-related areas such as equipment for the energy, chemical and shipbuilding industries, GS Global said. The company also seeks to strengthen collaboration with major Korean steelmakers that have operations near Houston, such as Hyundai Steel and Dongkuk Steel, while developing new business opportunities with local engineering, procurement and construction companies and steel fabricators. An opening ceremony for the Houston branch was held Tuesday. It was attended by Consulate General of Korea in Houston Lee Kyung-eun, Jindal Pipe USA President Vikas Chandra and representatives from Posco, Hyundai Steel, Korea National Oil Corporation and Hanwha Ocean. “The establishment of the Houston branch is a strategic investment aimed at expanding our direct engagement with customers in the U.S. market and strengthening our sales capabilities,” a GS Global spokesperson said. “We will solidify the foundation for sustainable growth in North America by pursuing new business opportunities across a range of areas, including project-based steel sales.” Samsung’s thinner, lighter Fold8 is drawing younger women and longtime Apple loyalists with record preorders and a passport-style design. title: $2.25 Billion Bold Bet: Goldman Sachs (GS.US) Acquires NEOS, Reshaping the Crypto Options Landscape - Moomoo
content: To create a seamless experience and for website quality and improvement purposes, we use cookie technologies for verification and quality purposes, to personalize the content presented, and to provide advertising that may be of specific interest to you. Learn our Privacy Policy here. Goldman Sachs plans to acquire NEOS for up to $2.25 billion, gaining access to 19 ETFs and $30 billion in assets under management (AUM). This move strengthens its positioning in Bitcoin and Ethereum options income strategies, distinguishing it from traditional spot ETFs. According to Woofun AI, Goldman Sachs (GS.US) officially announced an acquisition agreement with NEOS on August 12, marking a strategic shift for the Wall Street giant from simple crypto asset custody to a complex options-based business platform. The core of this transaction is not merely acquiring a cryptocurrency fund, but rather integrating NEOS's mature options ecosystem to build a comprehensive yield-generation system covering both traditional financial assets and digital assets. As the agreement was made public, market focus quickly shifted from the transaction amount itself to how Goldman Sachs plans to combine its vast client base with NEOS's unique options yield strategies to open new growth curves in the increasingly competitive ETF market. The financial structure of the deal is highly conditional and incentive-driven, with the acquisition consideration capped at $2.25 billion. The payment method includes cash and equity, with portions directly linked to future performance targets and service commitments. This means that $2.25 billion represents a theoretical valuation peak rather than a fixed cost. Based on this maximum amount, the transaction's valuation multiple is approximately 7.5% of NEOS's current assets under management (AUM), a ratio that appears relatively restrained yet highly targeted within the context of financial M&A. Subject to approvals from regulators such as the SEC and other customary closing conditions, the transaction is expected to close formally in the first quarter of 2027. As a key component of the deal, NEOS co-founders Troy Kacz and Garrett Polera will be promoted to partners at Goldman Sachs Asset Management post-closing, ensuring the stability of the core strategy team. Data compiled by Woofun AI shows that NEOS currently manages 19 ETFs with total AUM of approximately $30 billion. The vast majority of these products employ active management strategies aimed at generating excess returns through options instruments. Notably, NEOS's largest products are not cryptocurrency-related funds, but rather its traditional market offerings: the S&P 500 High Income ETF (SPYI) and the Nasdaq-100 High Income ETF (QQQI). By the end of July, AUM for these two funds had surpassed $10 billion and $13 billion, respectively. The remaining product line broadly covers small-cap equities, international stocks, real estate, bonds, U.S. Treasury notes, hedging strategies, and leveraged yield products, forming a diversified traditional asset yield matrix. Beyond its traditional business, Goldman Sachs gains a series of cryptocurrency-related products with proven operational expertise through this acquisition, most notably the NEOS Bitcoin High Income ETF (BTCI). BTCI's AUM has reached approximately $1.1 billion, making it a leading product in its category. Additionally, NEOS manages the Boosted Bitcoin High Income ETF (XBCI) and the Ethereum High Income ETF (NEHI). XBCI is designed to achieve yield levels approximately 150% of those generated by BTCI's corresponding strategy, while NEHI employs a similar yield-oriented options strategy tailored to the Ethereum market. These products present a stark structural contrast to BlackRock's (BLK.US) iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT.US). IBIT adopts a simple trust structure to hold Bitcoin directly, aiming purely to reflect its price volatility, and charges a 0.25% custody fee. In contrast, BTCI takes a distinctly different path; its annual operating expense ratio is 0.99%, and it does not hold Bitcoin spot directly. Instead, it constructs exposure through complex derivatives operations. The prospectus filed by BTCI with the SEC explicitly states that its core objective is to generate substantial monthly cash income by selling options while maintaining exposure to Bitcoin's appreciation potential. Specifically, the fund constructs a synthetic covered call strategy by purchasing call options with similar strike prices and expiration dates and selling put options, thereby simulating price exposure without actually holding Bitcoin. This mechanism allows the fund to generate cash flow through the decay of options' time value and the collection of premiums when Bitcoin prices rise moderately or trade sideways. However, if Bitcoin prices surge significantly beyond the relevant strike prices, the sold call options will begin to erode the capital appreciation gains achieved through long-term investment. The SEC clearly defines this approach as a "synthetic covered call strategy," the essence of which is trading part of the upside potential for deterministic monthly cash flows. Actual performance data for BTCI reveals the risk-return trade-off inherent in this strategy. As of June 30, BTCI's annualized distribution rate stood at 26.16%, while its 30-day SEC yield for the same period was 2.13%. However, the attractive high monthly distributions mask severe volatility in net asset value (NAV). Data shows that as of June 30, BTCI's one-year NAV total return, adjusted for distributions, was -40.9%. Bloomberg data shared by Eric Balchunas on August 11 further confirmed that, even accounting for subsequent market fluctuations, the loss over the one-year period remained approximately 42.5%. Although the fund distributes substantial cash to investors on a monthly basis, it cannot avoid a significant erosion of the overall principal. NEOS explains that these distributions are classified as return of capital for tax purposes, and their composition may include option premiums, dividends, capital gains, and interest. While this tax treatment of return of capital may offer certain tax advantages to investors, such as lowering the cost basis of the stock and thereby affecting the amount of gain or loss recognized upon future sale, it also means that the ostensibly high distribution rate does not accurately reflect actual investment performance. For U.S. investors, understanding the erosive effect of return of capital on the cost basis is crucial, as it directly impacts final after-tax returns. Unlike spot ETFs, BTCI’s return structure focuses more on generating regular cash flows rather than fully tracking every price rebound of Bitcoin. When Bitcoin prices surge sharply, the upside potential forgone by BTCI through selling call options may far exceed the income generated from the option strategy, causing its performance to lag significantly behind the spot price. Conversely, in market environments where Bitcoin prices move sideways or rise moderately, the advantages of the option strategy become apparent; even if call options expire without significant price appreciation, the premiums generated provide important support to final returns. However, this does not mean that sideways movement guarantees profitability; option pricing, holding costs, and minor fluctuations in the underlying asset price still exert complex influences on fund performance. More critically, BTCI remains exposed to the risk of declining Bitcoin prices. Its Bitcoin-related exposure shrinks as the market falls, and the hedging effect provided by call options is limited. In the event of a sharp market correction, option premiums accumulated over months could be wiped out instantly. BTCI’s performance over the past year is a typical example of this downside risk materializing rapidly; while investors enjoy high distributions, they must bear the cost of significant principal erosion. Goldman Sachs’ acquisition of NEOS is a key step in deepening its layout of option-based income products, rather than an isolated event. Goldman Sachs has already accumulated extensive experience with GPIX and GPIQ ETFs, which combine exposure to S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 assets with actively managed call option strategies, demonstrating its ability to generate income through options in traditional markets. In April this year, Goldman Sachs completed the acquisition of Innovator Capital Management, acquiring 171 fixed-income ETFs and approximately $31 billion in assets under management, showcasing its strategic preference for rapidly expanding its ETF footprint through mergers and acquisitions. The acquisition of NEOS brings Goldman Sachs an additional 19 operating ETFs with approximately $30 billion in assets under management, along with a professional team possessing mature products and strategies. Compared to launching new products from scratch and gradually building scale, directly acquiring mature products allows for rapid capture of market share. Market trends indicate that asset managers are increasingly utilizing option instruments to combine traditional asset exposure with monthly income, fixed buffer mechanisms, and leverage effects. The focus of competition has shifted from lowest-cost index tracking to the design of higher value-added income structures. A similar trend has emerged in the cryptocurrency sector: BlackRock launched its own Bitcoin premium income ETF in June, while Goldman Sachs filed an application for its proprietary Bitcoin premium income ETF in April. NEOS provides Goldman Sachs with live Bitcoin and Ethereum income products that already have a certain asset scale, enabling immediate entry into this fast-growing market segment. The first wave of spot Bitcoin ETFs addressed a fundamental question: How can investors gain Bitcoin exposure through brokerage accounts? Products like BTCI raise a deeper question: What role should this Bitcoin exposure actually play? Options can convert volatility into cash distributions, limit investors’ upside participation during price rebounds, increase leverage, or create more specific income structures. Although the ticker symbols for these products still reference Bitcoin, investors are no longer simply purchasing Bitcoin exposure, which alters the due diligence requirements investors must fulfill. For option-based cryptocurrency ETFs, understanding how income is constituted, its tax implications, and potential downside risks is as important as understanding the underlying assets. Through this acquisition, Goldman Sachs has not only acquired products but also gained the authority to define the investment logic for this emerging asset class. title: Karol G's 'No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto' Reviewed - Yahoo
content: Like the best artists, Karol G's career can be broken down into eras, from the bare, stripped down vibes of Ocean to the colorful, globe-spanning energy of Tropicoqueta—which came out last year. And so when she was sending out signs that she was going to put out another album, it seemed like again she was pivoting. During her record-breaking performance at Coachella in April she performed "Después de Ti," a slow-burn ballad with Cigarettes After Sex guitarist Greg Gonzalez. A couple of months later, she graced the cover of Elle, and in an interview insinuated that the album she was working on was going to be more emotive, saying "I'm inviting everyone to be a little more dramatic, a little more extra." She also revealed that she recorded the album in isolation in Hawaii. "In making this album, I put a lot into being alone," she said. "I did a lot of hiking alone. I would climb the mountains alone. I would stand there gazing at the sky. I learned a lot about enjoying my solitude in this industry—we are really, really lonely. Compared to the rest of the world, you're very isolated." A couple of weeks later, we get No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, her sixth studio album. (The album title translated into English is "I Don't Regret Feeling So Much.") And similar to what Karol has been saying, the album is a contemplative (but not always downbeat) collection of songs. The album features two of the biggest commercial superstars in music (Drake and Bruno Mars), and the perreo single "Matadora" is quite raunchy—but despite that, the album largely represents the late summer blues, down to the cover, which features a hazy, dusky blue, which seems indebted to Britney Spears' In the Zone. No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto is an old-school breakup album, one covering most of the stages of grief, from anger ("Te Llevas To'") to depression ("Final Feliz") to finally acceptance ("Eclipse"). (Although never mentioned by name, the assumption is the album is about the end of her relationship with Feid.) The album is a complete 180 from the colorful soundscape on Tropicoqueta. For artists, heartbreak is one of the most fertile fields to mine in. And it's been a while since we've gotten a major pop album this singularly focused on the theme. Where Karol benefits is that while the topic is consistent, the musical palettes are diverse enough to make heartbreak come in various different flavors. If you read the lyrics to songs like album opener "Te Llevas To" and "Bebiendo Lágrimas," you'd think you're getting ready for a crying season. But those songs are built around energetic productions—an EDM base for the former, a hypnotic reggaeton heater for the latter. Then there are the songs that are slower and more downbeat, most notably the devastating "Final Feliz," but even those have an alternative energy that keeps you on your toes. That song was produced by alt artist Oklou and has a similar whimsical, deconstructed sound that Karol effortlessly fits herself into. —Dimas Sanfiorenzo In the past, when we've heard Señor Drizzy cook en Español, it's been a pretty mixed bag. He sounded natural on Bad Bunny's "MIA," but he was straight-up cringe on "Meet Your Padres" with Chino Pacas. "Ahí" is one of his better showings—arguably the best Spanish performance of his career. After years of teased collabs, this is the first collaboration between the two, and it's mostly a winner. He delivers on all fronts: his pronunciation feels natural, and his lyricism actually has some emotional depth. "I don't want to pressure you at all. Don't worry, I'm here for you. / I'll wait for my moment, baby," he sings (translated from Spanish). Rather than sounding like a guest dropped into the song, Drake feels woven into it, stepping in and harmonizing with Karol on the chorus and bridge, over the tranquil Afro-reggaeton production. The song isn't perfect. The weakest part of his performance comes when he switches back to English and starts to call back to his song "New Bestie," resurrecting the "I want a Latina" line. It's a cute move, but one that feels too calculated in how it's trying to spark virality. —Antonio Johri Compared to the journey through Latin American folk music we received on Tropicoqueta, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto is a much more conservative take on Latin pop. Rather than continuing that experimentation, it feels like Karol is homing back in on the popetón formula that made Mañana Será Bonito so successful. Her go-to producer, Ovy on the Drums, brings back that familiar sound with tight drums and airy melodies across "Bebiendo Lágrimas," "Ahí," and "¿Con quién andará?" Tainy also lends a hand on the lead single "Matadora" and "BbY WOW," the latter of which samples "Coolie Dance Rhythm." It's one of the better uses of the sample, as they flip the familiar rhythm into a melancholy pop banger. She does venture out, though, hopping in her Selena bag with the more Tejano/cumbia-inspired "Alguien que te amaba." Karol sounds like a natural, with her powerful vocals shining over sparkly production. —Antonio Johri Maybe the most surprising moment on the album comes with "Still," an '80s-inspired emo duet with Bruno Mars. The song is fully in English and is one of the stronger cuts on the album, showcasing the natural chemistry the two have. The question, of course, is how much more English-language music is in Karol's future. In an interview with Rolling Stone, she spoke about the song, saying that even if a full-length English album seems out of the picture, she's down to doing more music in English. "I'm super open," she said. "The only thing I wouldn't do is sit down and try to do a whole album in English like, 'This is my English album.'"—Dimas Sanfiorenzo There is an argument to make that Karol G, who is currently in the middle of a stadium tour, is at her peak. Similar to how Bad Bunny leveraged his massive success and popularity to create an album that was personal and political, Karol seems to be doing her own version of this. No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto is the first on her imprint, Bichota Records, and it's a real show of strength. Despite the addictive and melodic nature of some of the songs (we didn't even talk about "¿Con quién andará?" yet!), the album is a headphone album during an era where she's making stadium music. Instead of taking the massive heights of her success and trying to scale that up, Karol made an album that was smaller and more intimate. It's a hell of a flex, one that we predict will even take her to higher heights. —Dimas Sanfiorenzo Karol G's New Album Features Drake in Their First-Ever Official Collab Karol G's 'No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto': Tracklist, Features, and Everything You Need to Know Karol G Surprises Married Couple With Honeymoon Trip to Her Paris Show Ken Carson Says He Has Never Drank Alcohol: 'That Kill a Lot' COMPLEX SHOP: Shop the brands you love, anytime and anywhere. (NYSE:GS)–NEOS deal looks strategically important because it pushes Goldman further into a part of asset management that is growing quickly: actively managed ETFs, particularly products that use options to generate income and manage downside risk. Goldman is paying up to $2.25 billion for NEOS, which manages about $30 billion across 19 ETFs. The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027. The biggest bullish argument is that The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) is building a more diversified and recurring asset-management business. NEOS gives Goldman exposure to income-oriented ETFs that are designed around options strategies. That could be attractive to investors looking for regular income and some downside protection, especially when market volatility remains elevated. Goldman said its asset and wealth management revenue rose 20% year over year to $4.6 billion in the second quarter, showing that this part of the business is already gaining momentum. The deal also builds on The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS)'s $2 billion acquisition of Innovator Capital Management, which closed in April 2026. Innovator brought Goldman roughly $31 billion in assets across defined-outcome ETFs. Adding NEOS should take Goldman's active ETF assets to around $80 billion, giving it considerably more scale in a rapidly expanding market. For Goldman shareholders, the longer-term benefit is less dependence on investment banking and trading. Those businesses can be highly profitable but are tied to deal activity and market conditions. Asset management can provide a steadier stream of fee revenue. The concern is that The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) may be paying a fairly high price to accelerate its ETF ambitions. The $2.25 billion maximum price represents roughly 7.5% of NEOS' $30 billion in assets under management. Reuters' Breakingviews noted that this looks expensive compared with the amount of assets Goldman is acquiring. There is also no guarantee that NEOS' rapid growth will continue. Options-based income ETFs have become popular, but competition is increasing. If more asset managers launch similar products, fees could come under pressure, and the returns of some strategies may become less compelling. The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (NYSE:GS) also has to integrate NEOS while digesting its earlier Innovator acquisition. If the firm cannot generate sufficient organic inflows or cross-selling opportunities, the deal could take longer than expected to earn an attractive return. JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE:JPM) is probably the most relevant comparison. Both firms are using their investment-management platforms to capitalize on the shift toward active ETFs rather than relying only on traditional mutual funds. JPMorgan entered the active ETF market earlier and has built a substantial franchise. The firm describes itself as the No. 1 global active ETF provider by assets under management, based on data as of the end of 2025. Its ETF business spans equity, fixed income, income, and other strategies. Goldman's approach is different. Rather than simply building a broad ETF lineup organically, it is using acquisitions to quickly add specialized capabilities. The Innovator and NEOS deals give Goldman expertise in defined-outcome, income, and options-based ETFs. That creates an interesting trade-off. JPMorgan has the advantage of an established active ETF platform, while Goldman is trying to close the gap through acquisitions. The strategy could work well if active ETFs continue taking market share. JPMorgan Chase & Co. (NYSE:JPM)'s own research shows that active ETFs already account for about 37% of ETF flows in 2026, highlighting the opportunity Goldman is targeting. (NYSE:JPM) at the end of Q1 2026, as per Insider Monkey's database. The consolidated value of these stakes is more than $15.5 billion. The company is buying into a fast-growing ETF segment and strengthening its asset-management business with products that can generate recurring fee revenue. If active and income-focused ETFs continue attracting investors, NEOS could become a meaningful contributor to Goldman's long-term growth. The main risk is that Goldman is paying a premium to accelerate that growth. With the earlier Innovator acquisition and now NEOS, the firm is making a sizable commitment to a competitive market. title: CSM Switches to Aston Martin for Rest of GS Season - Sportscar365
content: CSM adds second entry for Houk, Ellahi for final three races; enters GT4 America for Indy… Czabok-Simpson Motorsport has made the switch from Porsche to Aston Martin GT4 machinery for the remainder of the IMSA Michelin Pilot Challenge season, while adding a second GS class entry in the process. The Indianapolis-based team, which has long been affiliated with running Porsches, will field two Aston Martin Vantage GT4 Evos beginning with next weekend’s round at Virginia International Raceway. While Gordon Scully and Morgan Burkhard will remain together in the No. 2 entry, Ayrton Houk as Ismaeel Ellahi will team up in the No. 3 Aston Martin for a three-race Pilot Challenge program. The shift to the British manufacturer is being billed as a “strategic move” according to a team statement, in order to get a jump start on the 2027 season. Sportscar365 understands CSM acquired one of Rebel Rock Racing’s Astons that it previously ran in the series. “Moving both cars to the Aston Martin now is an important step in our preparation for 2027,” said team co-owner Stephen Simpson. “It gives our engineers and drivers three race weekends to build a meaningful base of knowledge in Michelin Pilot Challenge conditions. “Ayrton has already tested with us several times and has consistently impressed the team with his pace, feedback and approach. “Ismaeel’s development in such a short period has been exceptional, and his CTMP victory showed that he is ready for this next challenge. “Gordon and Morgan give us the experience and continuity we need, so we believe these lineups create a very strong foundation for the rest of this
